Static-analysis sweep of the Lantern-Plus frontend (src/features/**, src/platform/**) for a SECOND recurring bug class fixed repeatedly today: stale-async-closure-sets-state / request races. Pattern: an async operation (provider resolution, retrieval, a fetch, a workspace load) completes LATE and then sets React state, fires a confirm, or triggers a send — but the component/context has since CHANGED (user switched client/workspace/chat, or submitted a newer request), so the stale completion acts on the WRONG current state. Real examples fixed today: notice-trail loaded for meeting A still setNotices after switching to meeting B; a cancelled Ask still sent after provider resolution; a whole-practice question resolved late and could send against the CURRENT client set; an orphan-recovery filter compared paths in mismatched forms. HUNT for MORE: (1) async .then/await callbacks that call setState/setX without an if-still-current / request-token / cancelled guard; (2) effects with async work whose result sets state without checking the effect wasn't superseded (missing cleanup cancellation); (3) submit/confirm/send flows where an async step between click and action doesn't re-verify the target is still the same. For EACH: file:line, the exact wrong-target scenario (what stale value acts on what current state), and severity (P0 wrong-client-data / P1 broken / P2 wrong-state / P3). Rank by severity, focus P0/P1. READ-ONLY, change nothing. Write to /home/jameson/lantern-plus/coordination/qa-campaign/static-race-sweep.md if writable, else output the ranked list.

# LANTERN-PLUS — What this folder is (READ THIS FIRST)

**Created 2026-07-02 by Jameson's direction.** This is a **full, git-linked fork of Keepance**
(internally now called **Lantern**), branched from the true `keepance-3.0` tip
(`000060cf`, fetched fresh from GitHub) onto the branch **`lantern-plus`**.

**Status (2026-07-04): feature-complete.** All five waves (0-4) of the Jump
feature-parity program are merged, and the full real-Windows verification pass
has run clean — see `docs/PRODUCT-JOURNEY.md`'s 2026-07-04 entries for the
detailed story. Work in this folder now is QA, hardening, and cleanup, not new
feature waves.

## Why it exists

Two efforts run in parallel and must not collide:

1. **`~/keepance` (main folder)** — the standalone Lantern being hardened, demoed, and
   released. Another coordinator instance with subagents actively works there.
   **Never edit files in `~/keepance` from a Lantern-Plus session.**
2. **`~/lantern-plus` (this folder)** — builds the **Jump feature-parity program**:
   meeting capture, calendar → auto prep briefs, CRM write-back, and related features,
   per the feasibility assessment in [`feasibility/ASSESSMENT.md`](feasibility/ASSESSMENT.md).

## Ground rules for agents working here

- **Branch:** all work happens on `lantern-plus` (tracking `origin/keepance-3.0`) or
  feature branches off it (`lp/<feature>`), merged back into `lantern-plus`. Push to
  GitHub (`keepance/keepance`) freely; **never push to `keepance-3.0` itself** — that
  branch belongs to the main-line effort.
- **Stay mergeable:** prefer NEW modules/folders (`src/features/meetings/`,
  `src-tauri/src/commands/calendar/`, etc.) over edits to shared files. When a shared
  file must change, keep the diff minimal. Periodically
  `git fetch origin && git merge origin/keepance-3.0` into `lantern-plus` so drift
  stays small. Serialize merges; resolve conflicts in favor of main-line for
  everything outside this program's scope.
- **The plans are the spec:** [`docs/plans/lantern-plus/`](docs/plans/lantern-plus/)
  contains the master plan and per-wave implementation plans, written for Opus 4.8
  agents. Follow them; don't re-derive strategy.
- **All Keepance rules still apply** (CLAUDE.md in this repo): no shortcuts on core,
  gate before merge (`npm run gate`), never rename `matter_id`, no cloud paths for
  user content, only one cargo compile at a time (shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR).
- **Do not deploy or release from this folder.** Demo/release happens from the
  main-line effort. Lantern-Plus features reach users only by merging back after
  Jameson's go.

## Contents beyond the code fork

- [`feasibility/`](feasibility/) — the complete Jump feasibility assessment + research
  (moved here from `~/keepance-jump-feasibility`, now the canonical copy).
  Published report: https://jameworld.com/claudereports/r/2026-07-02-keepance-vs-jump-feature-parity-feasibility-assessment.html
- [`docs/plans/lantern-plus/`](docs/plans/lantern-plus/) — the implementation plans + the binding UI-INTEGRATION-SPEC + the NEXT-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP prompt (the deliverables of the Fable planning session).

## Open items (cross-lane dependencies)

Once Wave 3 merges into `lantern-plus`, mount `<SpeakerNamesPanel meetingDir={...} matterId={...} workspaceRoot={...} onApplied={reindex} />` in the transcript viewer per Wave 4 Track A Task 12 Step 6 (`docs/plans/lantern-plus/2026-07-02-wave-4-depth.md`).

The full chat sender has the same shape but worse: after the AI returns, it awaits citation verification and then writes the final answer. That verification uses the live selected client, and there is no “am I still on the same chat/client?” check before committing.

I’m being careful not to over-call normal “old request finishes in its own old chat” as a bug. The bug class only matters when the old request can touch the new screen, new client, or new request. I’m checking store reads and workspace wiring next, because those often read “whatever is current now.”

   662	 * QA-19: a single watcher-triggered index attempt used to be fire-and-forget
   663	 * with no retry — a transient failure (e.g. a read racing the tail end of an
   664	 * autosave write, or a lock held a moment too long) permanently dropped that
   665	 * file from search until the next full boot reconcile. These are the delays
   666	 * between retries; two retries at a short, then a longer, interval is enough
   667	 * to ride out a write-in-flight race without turning a genuinely bad file
   668	 * into an infinite retry loop.
   669	 */
   670	export const INDEX_FILE_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [300, 1000];
   671	
   672	export type IndexRetryScheduler = {
   673	  /** Index `path`, retrying with backoff on failure. */
   674	  schedule: (path: string) => void;
   675	  /**
   676	   * Cancel every pending retry timer WITHOUT running it. Must be called on
   677	   * workspace close/switch (see the per-workspace effect's cleanup) — a
   678	   * scheduled retry captures only a plain file path, not which workspace it
   679	   * belonged to, and `MemoryService.indexFile` always targets whatever
   680	   * workspace is CURRENTLY active on the Rust side. An uncancelled retry that
   681	   * fires after a switch would therefore index an OLD workspace's file
   682	   * straight into the NEW workspace's search index — a cross-client content
   683	   * leak. (Flagged by codex-review on the first cut of this fix, which left
   684	   * retries running forever with no cancellation handle.)
   685	   */
   686	  disposeAll: () => void;
   687	};
   688	
   689	/**
   690	 * Create a scheduler that (re)indexes a file, retrying with backoff on
   691	 * failure before giving up and logging loudly. One instance is owned per
   692	 * workspace mount so its retries can be cancelled wholesale on close/switch
   693	 * — see {@link IndexRetryScheduler.disposeAll}.
   694	 */
   695	export function createIndexRetryScheduler(): IndexRetryScheduler {
   696	  const timers = new Set<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();
   697	  let disposed = false;
   698	
   699	  const attempt = (path: string, retryCount: number): void => {
   700	    MemoryService.indexFile(path).catch((err: unknown) => {
   701	      if (disposed) return;
   702	      if (retryCount < INDEX_FILE_RETRY_DELAYS_MS.length) {
   703	        const timer = setTimeout(() => {
   704	          timers.delete(timer);
   705	          attempt(path, retryCount + 1);
   706	        }, INDEX_FILE_RETRY_DELAYS_MS[retryCount]);
   707	        timers.add(timer);
   708	      } else {
   709	        console.error(
   710	          `[memory] failed to index ${path} after ${String(retryCount + 1)} attempts; ` +
   711	            'it will be picked up by the next reconcile instead',
   712	          err,
   713	        );
   714	      }
   715	    });
   716	  };
   717	
   718	  return {
   719	    schedule(path: string) {
   720	      attempt(path, 0);
   721	    },
   722	    disposeAll() {
   723	      disposed = true;
   724	      timers.forEach((timer) => {
   725	        clearTimeout(timer);
   726	      });
   727	      timers.clear();
   728	    },
   729	  };
   730	}

   732	/**
   733	 * Route one `workspace-file-changed` event: buffer deletes through the burst
   734	 * batcher, and for a create/modify, first cancel any delete still queued for
   735	 * the same path (the delete→recreate race guard — see
   736	 * createDeleteBurstBatcher) before (re)indexing it. Extracted out of the
   737	 * `listen()` callback so the race guard is unit-testable without standing up
   738	 * the full Tauri event-listener machinery.
   739	 */
   740	export function handleWorkspaceFileChangedEvent(
   840	): string[] {
   841	  const changed = new Set<string>();
   842	  for (const key of Object.keys(next)) {
   843	    if (prev[key] !== next[key]) changed.add(key);
   844	  }
   845	  for (const key of Object.keys(prev)) {
   846	    if (!(key in next)) changed.add(key); // privilege cleared back to "none"
   847	  }
   848	  return Array.from(changed);
   849	}

   851	/**
   852	 * WS-B/C — re-index all files under the changed folders using the current
   853	 * source of truth. When the workspace service exposes `getFileTree`, a fresh
   854	 * disk scan is performed so externally-added files (not yet reflected in the
   855	 * cached in-memory tree) are included. Falls back to the cached tree in
   856	 * browser / test mode or when the disk scan fails. Exported for unit testing.

   859	 * group to `MemoryService.reindexPaths`, which handles per-file privilege

   863	  folders: string[],
   864	  workspaceService: MemoryWiringWorkspaceService | null | undefined,
   865	): Promise<void> {
   866	  const allPaths = collectAllFilePaths(await getFreshOrCachedFileTree(workspaceService));
   867	
   868	  const { rootPath } = useWorkspaceStore.getState();
   869	  const affected = allPaths.filter((p) => pathInAnyFolder(p, folders, rootPath));

   875	  // resolution uses the workspace-relative path, then the backend receives the
   876	  // absolute path shape the Rust full-workspace walk stores.
   877	  const byMatter = new Map<string, string[]>();

   879	    const id = resolveMatterIdForWorkspacePath(p, rootPath);
   880	    const list = byMatter.get(id) ?? [];
   881	    list.push(buildWorkspaceAbsolutePath(rootPath, p));
   882	    byMatter.set(id, list);
   883	  }
   884	  for (const [matterId, paths] of byMatter) {
   885	    await MemoryService.reindexPaths(paths, matterId);
   886	  }

   888	  if (!isPdfIndexingEnabled() || !workspaceService) return;
   889	  const binaryWs = buildBinaryWorkspace(workspaceService);
   890	  if (!binaryWs) return;
   891	  for (const path of pdfPaths) {
   892	    try {
   893	      await MemoryService.indexPdfFile(buildWorkspaceAbsolutePath(rootPath, path), binaryWs);
   894	    } catch {
   895	      // Best-effort: skip individual failures, continue with the rest.
   896	    }
   897	  }
   898	}

   900	/** Walk all .pdf files in the workspace and index them via MemoryService. */
   901	export async function indexWorkspacePdfs(
   902	  workspaceService: MemoryWiringWorkspaceService,
   903	): Promise<void> {
   904	  const binaryWs = buildBinaryWorkspace(workspaceService);
   905	  if (!binaryWs) return;
   906	  const { rootPath } = useWorkspaceStore.getState();
   907	  // Retry the FRESH scan until the workspace backend is initialized and the tree
   908	  // is loaded, so PDFs index reliably even when the index fires immediately on
   909	  // open (the empty-cached-tree race that previously dropped ~80% of files).
   910	  const pdfPaths = collectPdfPaths(await getFreshTreeWithRetry(workspaceService));
   911	  if (pdfPaths.length === 0) return;
   912	  const progress = usePdfIndexProgressStore.getState();
   913	  progress.set({ processed: 0, total: pdfPaths.length, currentPath: null });
   914	  // P1.1 (Task 3): whether OCR is on is part of a PDF's freshness signature, so
   915	  // read it once and pass it to the manifest fresh-check below.
   916	  const ocrEnabled = isOcrScannedPdfsEnabled();
   917	  for (const [index, path] of pdfPaths.entries()) {
   918	    const ragPath = buildWorkspaceAbsolutePath(rootPath, path);
   919	    progress.set({ processed: index, total: pdfPaths.length, currentPath: ragPath });
   920	    try {
   921	      // P1.1 (Task 3): skip a PDF whose size/mtime + OCR setting are unchanged
   922	      // since it was last indexed — PDF extraction + OCR is the single most
   923	      // expensive per-file cost, so this is the biggest boot win for PDF-heavy
   924	      // workspaces. A new/changed/tombstoned PDF returns false and re-indexes.
   925	      if (await ragManifestPdfFresh(ragPath, ocrEnabled)) {
   926	        continue;
   927	      }
   928	      await MemoryService.indexPdfFile(ragPath, binaryWs);
   929	    } catch {
   930	      // Best-effort: skip individual failures, continue with the rest.
   931	    } finally {
   932	      progress.set({ processed: index + 1, total: pdfPaths.length, currentPath: ragPath });
   933	    }
   934	  }
   935	  progress.clearSoon();
   936	}

   938	/**
   939	 * P1.1 — apply each mapped folder's matter (and privilege) to its files' EXISTING
   940	 * rows IN PLACE, WITHOUT re-embedding. A cheap SQL column update per file.

   943	 * reconcile already (re)indexed every new/changed file — new ones under the
   944	 * UNASSIGNED default — so on boot the files under a client folder already have
   945	 * rows; they just need the folder's matter applied. Re-embedding them (the old
   946	 * boot behaviour) redid the single most expensive step on EVERY warm boot of any
   947	 * workspace WITH client mappings, defeating the reconcile's whole win. In-place
   948	 * retag moves them to the right scope for pennies. (Explicit folder-mapping
   949	 * changes still go through `reindexFolderPaths`, which also indexes not-yet-
   950	 * indexed files — a deliberate one-off, not a per-boot cost.)
   951	 */
   952	async function retagFolderPathsInPlace(
   953	  folders: string[],
   954	  workspaceService: MemoryWiringWorkspaceService | null | undefined,
   955	): Promise<void> {
   956	  const allPaths = collectAllFilePaths(await getFreshOrCachedFileTree(workspaceService));
   957	  const { rootPath } = useWorkspaceStore.getState();
   958	  const affected = allPaths.filter((p) => pathInAnyFolder(p, folders, rootPath));
   959	
   960	  // Group by resolved matter so each matter's files retag in ONE batched UPDATE.
   961	  // LanceDB rewrites data per UPDATE, so a per-file retag loop is ~as slow as
   962	  // re-embedding — batching per matter collapses it to one rewrite per matter.
   963	  const byMatter = new Map<string, string[]>();
   964	  const privileged: Array<{ abs: string; privilege: string }> = [];
   965	  for (const p of affected) {
   966	    const abs = buildWorkspaceAbsolutePath(rootPath, p);
   967	    const matterId = resolveMatterIdForWorkspacePath(p, rootPath);
   968	    const list = byMatter.get(matterId);
   969	    if (list) list.push(abs);
   970	    else byMatter.set(matterId, [abs]);
   971	    // Only privileged sources need a privilege retag — the common 'none' default
   972	    // is already correct, so we skip it (and keep those few per-file).
   973	    const privilege = resolvePrivilegeForSource(abs);

   979	      // a no-op; the reconcile/watcher indexes them.
   980	      await MemoryService.retagMatterBatch(paths, matterId);
   981	    } catch {
   982	      // Best-effort: skip and continue with the next matter.
   983	    }
   984	  }
   985	  for (const { abs, privilege } of privileged) {
   986	    try {
   987	      await MemoryService.retagPrivilege(abs, privilege);
   988	    } catch {
   989	      // Best-effort.
   990	    }
   991	  }
   992	}

   994	export async function retagExistingMatterFolderPaths(

   130	// ── downloadBase64File — browser-side blob download, no disk persistence ───
   131	
   132	function downloadBase64File(filename: string, contentType: string, bytesBase64: string) {
   133	  const byteChars = atob(bytesBase64);
   134	  const byteNums = new Array(byteChars.length).fill(0).map((_, i) => byteChars.charCodeAt(i));
   135	  const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(byteNums)], { type: contentType });
   136	  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
   137	  const a = document.createElement('a');
   138	  a.href = url;
   139	  a.download = filename;
   140	  a.click();
   141	  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
   142	}

    61	export function useApiKeys(keychainService?: ApiKeyKeychain): UseApiKeysReturn {
    62	  const [apiKeys, setApiKeys] = useState<APIKey[]>([]);
    63	  // Mirrors `apiKeys` so loadKeys() (below) can fall back to "what we already
    64	  // had" for a provider whose read failed/timed out, instead of treating a
    65	  // transient keychain hiccup as "key removed".

    72	  // Memoized so the load effect below doesn't re-run on every render.
    73	  const keychain = useMemo<ApiKeyKeychain>(
    74	    () => keychainService ?? createKeychainService(),
    75	    [keychainService]
    76	  );

    78	  // Save: persist through the keychain first (validates the format, stores in
    79	  // the OS keychain / obfuscated localStorage, and notifies the egress badge),
    80	  // then mirror into in-memory session state. If setKey throws (bad format /
    81	  // keychain failure), we surface the error and leave state untouched.

    87	        if (existing) {

    89	            k.provider === provider ? { ...k, key, isValid: true, lastValidated: new Date() } : k
    90	          );
    91	        }
    92	        return [...prev, { provider, key, isValid: true, lastValidated: new Date() }];
    93	      });
    94	    },
    95	    [keychain]
    96	  );
    97	
    98	  // Delete: remove from the keychain (also notifies the egress badge), then
    99	  // drop it from in-memory state.
   100	  const handleDeleteApiKey = useCallback(
   101	    async (provider: KeyProvider) => {
   102	      await keychain.deleteKey(provider);

   104	    },
   105	    [keychain]
   106	  );

   110	  //
   111	  // Each provider is read independently (timeout + catch) so a hung or
   112	  // erroring OS keychain for one provider can't (a) block the others behind
   113	  // it, or (b) throw out of loadKeys() entirely and leave the app silently

   117	  // as "not configured" — otherwise a transient/timed-out keychain hiccup on

   120	  // through handleDeleteApiKey, which updates state directly, not loadKeys().
   121	  const loadKeys = useCallback(async (): Promise<{
   122	    keys: APIKey[];
   123	    credentialServiceUnavailable: boolean;
   124	  }> => {
   125	    let credentialServiceUnavailable = false;

   127	      PROVIDERS.map(async (provider): Promise<APIKey | null> => {
   128	        try {
   129	          const key = await withTimeout(
   130	            keychain.getKey(provider),
   131	            LOAD_KEY_TIMEOUT_MS,
   132	            `Reading the ${provider} key`,
   133	          );

   135	        } catch (err) {

   191	  return {
   192	    apiKeys,
   193	    handleSaveApiKey,
   194	    handleDeleteApiKey,
   195	    credentialServiceUnavailable,
   196	  };
   197	}

89 src/features/matters/MatterNotesEditorWrapper.tsx
/**
 * MatterNotesEditorWrapper — resolves the matter from the store and manages the
 * MatterSyncClient lifecycle for the notes tab.
 *
 * This is the React boundary between the tab system (which knows only the
 * localMatterId string) and the MatterNotesEditor (which needs the resolved
 * Matter object + a running MatterSyncClient). It boots the sync client on
 * mount and stops it when the tab unmounts.
 */

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { useMatterStore } from '@/platform/matter/matterStore';
import { ensureMatterSync, getMatterSyncClient } from '@/features/matters/logic/matterNotesSync';
import { MatterNotesEditor } from '@/features/matters/MatterNotesEditor';
import { useMatterSyncStatus } from '@/platform/matter/matterSyncStore';
import type { MatterSyncClient } from '@/platform/firm/MatterSyncClient';

interface MatterNotesEditorWrapperProps {
  localMatterId: string;
  workspaceService?: { writeFile: (path: string, content: string) => Promise<void> } | null;
  className?: string;
}

export function MatterNotesEditorWrapper({
  localMatterId,
  workspaceService,
  className,
}: MatterNotesEditorWrapperProps) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const matter = useMatterStore((s) => s.matters.find((m) => m.id === localMatterId) ?? null);
  const [syncClient, setSyncClient] = useState<MatterSyncClient | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  // Subscribe to sync status so we detect when stopMatterSync evicts our client
  // (e.g. after a key-epoch advance fails with 403/walled).
  const syncStatus = useMatterSyncStatus(localMatterId);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!matter) {
      setLoading(false);
      return;
    }
    let cancelled = false;
    // Only show the loading spinner on the initial mount or when our client has
    // been evicted from the cache (e.g. after a walled key-epoch advance). For
    // normal status transitions (connecting → live) the current syncClient is
    // still valid and we don't want to flash the loading state.
    const cachedClient = getMatterSyncClient(matter.id);
    if (!cachedClient) {
      setLoading(true);
    }
    void ensureMatterSync(matter).then((client) => {
      if (cancelled) return;
      setSyncClient(client);
      setLoading(false);
    });
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      // Do NOT stop the client on unmount — the notes tab can be closed and
      // re-opened; the singleton cache in matterNotesSync handles reuse.
      // stopMatterSync is called explicitly on unshare / sign-out.
    };
  }, [matter?.id, syncStatus]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  if (loading) {
    return (
      <div className={`flex items-center justify-center h-full text-muted-foreground text-sm ${className ?? ''}`}>
        <span>{t('matter.notes.loading')}</span>
      </div>
    );
  }

  if (!matter) {
    return (
      <div className={`flex items-center justify-center h-full text-muted-foreground text-sm ${className ?? ''}`}>
        <span>{t('matter.notes.not-found')}</span>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <MatterNotesEditor
      matter={matter}
      syncClient={syncClient}
      {...(workspaceService != null ? { workspaceService } : {})}
      {...(className != null ? { className } : {})}
    />
  );
}

**Findings**

1. **P0 — workspace search/index can mix old workspace files with the new workspace**
   [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:862), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:901), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:1014), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:1370)
   Scenario: old workspace A starts full/PDF/folder reindexing. User switches to workspace B while file-tree reads or full-index awaits are still running. Helpers later read `useWorkspaceStore.getState().rootPath` / `getMatters()` / `MemoryService` current workspace, so A’s paths can be rebuilt under B’s current root/search index.
   Fix: pass the captured `rootPath` into `reindexFolderPaths`, `indexWorkspacePdfs`, `retagFolderPathsInPlace`, `startFullIndex`; add a cancellation/generation check after every await before any `MemoryService.*` write.

2. **P0 — slower workspace open can overwrite the newer selected workspace**
   [WorkspaceSelector.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/documents/workspace/WorkspaceSelector.tsx:247), [WorkspaceSelector.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/documents/workspace/WorkspaceSelector.tsx:308)
   Scenario: user opens workspace A, then quickly opens B. If A’s load finishes last, it still calls `setRootPath`, `setFileTree`, `addRecentWorkspace`, and `onWorkspaceSelected`, making the app land on the wrong workspace.
   Fix: add an `openRequestIdRef`; increment at open start; before lines 320-328, return unless this is still the latest request.

3. **P0 — email A filing/draft can update email B’s viewer**
   [EmailViewer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/email/EmailViewer.tsx:241), [EmailViewer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/email/EmailViewer.tsx:261)
   Scenario: user files email A to a client or starts “Draft with AI,” then opens email B before the async work returns. Filing uses `setMessage(prev => ...)`, so it can mark B as filed to A’s chosen client. Drafting can set A’s reply draft in B’s reply box.
   Fix: capture `sourceId`/`message.id` at action start and check it is still current before `setMessage`, `setReplyDraft`, errors, and loading flags.

4. **P0 — voiceprints for client A can appear on client B**
   [VoiceprintsCard.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/matters/VoiceprintsCard.tsx:17), [VoiceprintsCard.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/matters/VoiceprintsCard.tsx:21)
   Scenario: `voiceprintList(workspaceRoot, matterId)` for A finishes after switching to B and calls `setItems`. B can show A’s biometric voice profiles. If the stale confirm state survives, delete can act with mismatched `matterId`/voiceprint id.
   Fix: add effect cancellation/request token, clear `items` and `confirming` on `workspaceRoot`/`matterId` change, and bind `matterId` into the pending delete object.

5. **P0/P1 — Ask can show old client answer after switching during email-citation labeling**
   [useAsk.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/useAsk.ts:1120), [useAsk.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/useAsk.ts:1191)
   Scenario: Ask checks `abort.signal.aborted` after provider response, then awaits `resolveEmailCitationLabels`. If the user switches client/chat during that await, cleanup aborts, but the code does not re-check before `addMessage`, `setTurns`, `setStreamingTurn`, and `setStatus`.
   Fix: add `if (abort.signal.aborted) return;` immediately after citation-label resolution and before all final state writes.

6. **P1 — citation verification result can paint onto the wrong citation card**
   [SourcePanel.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/SourcePanel.tsx:130)
   Scenario: user verifies source A, then the card rerenders for source B before `ragVerifyCitation` returns. A’s verdict can become B’s green/red status.
   Fix: capture `{id, matterId, excerpt}` or a request token; only `setVerdict` if the card still represents the same citation.

7. **P1 — privilege explainer can report proof for the wrong current question/client**
   [PrivilegeExclusionExplainer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/PrivilegeExclusionExplainer.tsx:72)
   Scenario: demo runs retrieval for query/scope A, user changes question/client/scope while it is running, late result displays as if it applies to the new context.
   Fix: token per demo run, or compare current `trimmedQuery` + serialized `scope` before `setDemo`.

8. **P1/P2 — Memory facts settings can show stale workspace facts**
   [MemoryFactsSettings.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/settings/MemoryFactsSettings.tsx:55)
   Scenario: `svc.listFacts()` for workspace A returns after facts service has switched to workspace B, then `setFacts` shows A’s memory facts in B’s settings.
   Fix: capture service/workspace generation and drop stale refresh results; guard `handleAdd`/`handleDelete` refresh similarly.

9. **P2 — Run-on-all contradiction analysis can attach to a later comparison**
   [RunOnAllButton.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/chat/RunOnAllButton.tsx:123), [RunOnAllButton.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/chat/RunOnAllButton.tsx:167)
   Scenario: first comparison finishes results, starts slow contradiction analysis; user starts another comparison; old analysis can set `analysis` during/after the new run.
   Fix: request id around both `setResults` and `setAnalysis`.

Recommended overall patch shape: use a small standard pattern everywhere: `const requestId = ++ref.current`, capture the target ids at start, and after every `await` that precedes state/store writes, return unless `requestId === ref.current` and the target ids still match. For workspace indexing, do not read global current root after awaits; pass the captured root through.

**Findings**

1. **P0 — workspace search/index can mix old workspace files with the new workspace**
   [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:862), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:901), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:1014), [useMemoryWiring.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/platform/hooks/useMemoryWiring.ts:1370)
   Scenario: old workspace A starts full/PDF/folder reindexing. User switches to workspace B while file-tree reads or full-index awaits are still running. Helpers later read `useWorkspaceStore.getState().rootPath` / `getMatters()` / `MemoryService` current workspace, so A’s paths can be rebuilt under B’s current root/search index.
   Fix: pass the captured `rootPath` into `reindexFolderPaths`, `indexWorkspacePdfs`, `retagFolderPathsInPlace`, `startFullIndex`; add a cancellation/generation check after every await before any `MemoryService.*` write.

2. **P0 — slower workspace open can overwrite the newer selected workspace**
   [WorkspaceSelector.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/documents/workspace/WorkspaceSelector.tsx:247), [WorkspaceSelector.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/documents/workspace/WorkspaceSelector.tsx:308)
   Scenario: user opens workspace A, then quickly opens B. If A’s load finishes last, it still calls `setRootPath`, `setFileTree`, `addRecentWorkspace`, and `onWorkspaceSelected`, making the app land on the wrong workspace.
   Fix: add an `openRequestIdRef`; increment at open start; before lines 320-328, return unless this is still the latest request.

3. **P0 — email A filing/draft can update email B’s viewer**
   [EmailViewer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/email/EmailViewer.tsx:241), [EmailViewer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/email/EmailViewer.tsx:261)
   Scenario: user files email A to a client or starts “Draft with AI,” then opens email B before the async work returns. Filing uses `setMessage(prev => ...)`, so it can mark B as filed to A’s chosen client. Drafting can set A’s reply draft in B’s reply box.
   Fix: capture `sourceId`/`message.id` at action start and check it is still current before `setMessage`, `setReplyDraft`, errors, and loading flags.

4. **P0 — voiceprints for client A can appear on client B**
   [VoiceprintsCard.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/matters/VoiceprintsCard.tsx:17), [VoiceprintsCard.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/matters/VoiceprintsCard.tsx:21)
   Scenario: `voiceprintList(workspaceRoot, matterId)` for A finishes after switching to B and calls `setItems`. B can show A’s biometric voice profiles. If the stale confirm state survives, delete can act with mismatched `matterId`/voiceprint id.
   Fix: add effect cancellation/request token, clear `items` and `confirming` on `workspaceRoot`/`matterId` change, and bind `matterId` into the pending delete object.

5. **P0/P1 — Ask can show old client answer after switching during email-citation labeling**
   [useAsk.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/useAsk.ts:1120), [useAsk.ts](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/useAsk.ts:1191)
   Scenario: Ask checks `abort.signal.aborted` after provider response, then awaits `resolveEmailCitationLabels`. If the user switches client/chat during that await, cleanup aborts, but the code does not re-check before `addMessage`, `setTurns`, `setStreamingTurn`, and `setStatus`.
   Fix: add `if (abort.signal.aborted) return;` immediately after citation-label resolution and before all final state writes.

6. **P1 — citation verification result can paint onto the wrong citation card**
   [SourcePanel.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/SourcePanel.tsx:130)
   Scenario: user verifies source A, then the card rerenders for source B before `ragVerifyCitation` returns. A’s verdict can become B’s green/red status.
   Fix: capture `{id, matterId, excerpt}` or a request token; only `setVerdict` if the card still represents the same citation.

7. **P1 — privilege explainer can report proof for the wrong current question/client**
   [PrivilegeExclusionExplainer.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/PrivilegeExclusionExplainer.tsx:72)
   Scenario: demo runs retrieval for query/scope A, user changes question/client/scope while it is running, late result displays as if it applies to the new context.
   Fix: token per demo run, or compare current `trimmedQuery` + serialized `scope` before `setDemo`.

8. **P1/P2 — Memory facts settings can show stale workspace facts**
   [MemoryFactsSettings.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/settings/MemoryFactsSettings.tsx:55)
   Scenario: `svc.listFacts()` for workspace A returns after facts service has switched to workspace B, then `setFacts` shows A’s memory facts in B’s settings.
   Fix: capture service/workspace generation and drop stale refresh results; guard `handleAdd`/`handleDelete` refresh similarly.

9. **P2 — Run-on-all contradiction analysis can attach to a later comparison**
   [RunOnAllButton.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/chat/RunOnAllButton.tsx:123), [RunOnAllButton.tsx](/home/jameson/lantern-plus/src/features/ask/chat/RunOnAllButton.tsx:167)
   Scenario: first comparison finishes results, starts slow contradiction analysis; user starts another comparison; old analysis can set `analysis` during/after the new run.
   Fix: request id around both `setResults` and `setAnalysis`.

Recommended overall patch shape: use a small standard pattern everywhere: `const requestId = ++ref.current`, capture the target ids at start, and after every `await` that precedes state/store writes, return unless `requestId === ref.current` and the target ids still match. For workspace indexing, do not read global current root after awaits; pass the captured root through.
